data_scope: SAMPLE MODE - deterministic 10,000-ride sample; NOT the complete dataset. Values are not representative.

definition.name: Median request-to-pickup time
definition.grain: one completed HVFHV ride; published per month
definition.population: in_kpi_population: request, pickup, dropoff present; pickup >= request; dropoff > pickup
definition.source: HVFHV trip records: request_datetime, pickup_datetime, dropoff_datetime
definition.exclusions: rides flagged pickup_before_request, dropoff_not_after_pickup or missing_timestamp (flagged, not deleted)
definition.interpretation: Typical time a rider waits between asking for a ride and being picked up.
definition.limitation: Request-to-pickup time, NOT driver wait time. For unflagged pre-scheduled rides request_datetime may be the booked slot (UNKNOWN; bounded by the sensitivity analysis). Completed trips only.

definition.name: P90 request-to-pickup time
definition.grain: one completed HVFHV ride; published per month
definition.interpretation: Reliability: 1 in 10 riders waits at least this long. The tail a median hides.
definition.limitation: Same as KPI 1; the tail is the part most exposed to unflagged scheduled rides.

definition.name: Driver-arrival share of request-to-pickup time
definition.numerator: total minutes from request until the driver is on scene
definition.denominator: total minutes from request until pickup
definition.grain: all qualifying rides in the month (ratio of sums)
definition.population: in_stage_population: KPI population AND request <= on_scene < pickup (on-scene independently observed)
definition.source: HVFHV trip records: request_datetime, on_scene_datetime, pickup_datetime
definition.exclusions: rides whose on_scene equals pickup to the second, precedes the request, or follows pickup
definition.interpretation: How much of the rider's wait is spent waiting for the driver to arrive (dispatch + travel) versus the driver waiting at the curb. Tells operations which stage to act on.
definition.limitation: Computed on the subset of rides with an observed on-scene event (the subset is published). That subset excludes rides whose on_scene equals pickup to the second - exactly the rides with no curb wait, whose arrival share would be 100% - so the published share is a LOWER BOUND on the driver-arrival share of the wait. Withheld automatically if the subset falls below the configured share.

definition.name: P90 request-to-pickup time by pickup zone
definition.formula: 90th percentile of (pickup - request) per PULocationID, labelled via the taxi zone lookup
definition.population: in_zone_population (KPI population with an attributable NYC pickup zone); zones with fewer than min_rides_per_zone rides are listed but not ranked
definition.source: HVFHV PULocationID + request/pickup timestamps; Taxi Zone Lookup
definition.exclusions: placeholder zone IDs 264/265 (Unknown / Outside of NYC); IDs absent from the lookup
definition.interpretation: Where the poor-tail pickup experience is concentrated, so supply positioning can be targeted.
definition.limitation: Zone differences mix supply, demand, geography and trip mix: descriptive, not causal.

value.denominator_note: all zone-attributable pickups (includes rides flagged by the lifecycle rules); the P90 column in the borough table uses the KPI population instead

definition.name: Passenger FHV complaints to 311 per 100,000 HVFHV rides
definition.formula: 100000 * passenger_complaints / hvfhv_pickups, citywide and per borough
definition.numerator: 311 'For Hire Vehicle Complaint' records with descriptor 'Driver Complaint - Passenger' or 'Car Service Company Complaint', created in the month, mapped to a taxi zone
definition.denominator: HVFHV rides picked up in an attributable NYC zone in the same month (same geography). NOTE: this denominator is all zone-attributable pickups, including rides flagged by the lifecycle rules; the p90_request_to_pickup_min shown next to it in the borough table is computed on the KPI population (in_zone_population), a slightly smaller set. The two columns answer different questions on purpose.
definition.grain: borough per month (headline) - zone-level counts are published as supporting detail only
definition.population: all mapped passenger complaints; all zone-attributable HVFHV pickups
definition.source: NYC 311 Service Requests (Socrata erm2-nwe9), TLC taxi zone shapefile, HVFHV trips
definition.exclusions: non-passenger complaints (street safety, 81% of FHV complaints); complaints without coordinates or outside all zones (counted in validation, not guessed). Unmapped PASSENGER complaints are therefore missing from the numerator: the count and the resulting understatement are published as passenger_complaints_unmapped / rate_understatement_pct on this KPI
definition.interpretation: A contextual customer-friction signal: where riders escalate problems to the city. Read next to KPI 4 to see whether slow-pickup areas also generate more rider complaints.
definition.limitation: NOT a ride-level interaction: 311 has no ride ID and is never linked to a ride. Covers all FHV types (not only HVFHV), reflects the propensity to call 311, and is sparse - monthly zone-level rates are too noisy to rank, hence borough grain.

precipitation_association.conclusion: Demoted from KPI: hour-matched differences are ~0.1 min, no operational signal this month. Association only; one grid point represents all of NYC.

sensitivity_scheduled_rides.question: Are unflagged pre-scheduled rides distorting request-to-pickup time?
sensitivity_scheduled_rides.method: recompute KPI 1/2 excluding rides whose request timestamp is on an exact minute
sensitivity_scheduled_rides.note: Over-excludes (1 in 60 ordinary requests land on :00 by chance); it bounds the effect.

nyc311_composition.note: Non-passenger complaints (street safety) are excluded from KPI 5. Pickup-reliability reasons (refused pick-up, denied request, no-show) are too few to publish as their own metric.
